A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Path-of-Thoughts (PoT) research. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, graph-extraction experiments, and synthetic-noise evaluations in Tables 1–2, Figure 2, and appendix Table 28.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, computational-cost measurements, path-identification ablations, and path-count analyses in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The default graph-extraction, path-identification, and reasoning pipeline is unchanged, as are the appendix prompt templates. Section 4.2 newly identifies the path-finding algorithm as depth-first search; this specifies an existing component rather than establishing a procedural change. Shortest-path and path-removal variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use StepGame, CLUTRR, SPARTUN Find Relation questions, and the Chinese kinship dataset, together with the synthetic extraction test and seven graph-noise scenarios. Additional backbones and analyses operate within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster remains IO/Zero-shot, Few-shot, CoT, CoT-SC, and LLM-ASP. v2 adds internal comparison variants: PoT with path identification removed in Table 6 and shortest-path-only reasoning in Table 7. Figure 2 retains the earlier noise comparison under symbolic-reasoner-with/without-path-identification labels.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands model configurations with Llama3-70B-Instruct, o1-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, and GPT-5 at minimal and medium reasoning effort. It adds module-level latency and token measurements on GPT-4o StepGame k=3, plus path-removal and shortest-path controls. Existing benchmark sizes, preprocessing, and accuracy definitions are retained; these additions do not establish reruns of the earlier results.

E4.justification: New Table 6 directly tests removing path identification from both PoT variants. Appendix A.2/Table 7 analyzes path-count distributions and compares multiple paths against the shortest path alone. Table 25 adds an extraction-error example, and Table 26 introduces reasoning-error cases. The earlier extraction-prompt comparison and synthetic-noise analysis remain.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 introduce paired McNemar significance annotations comparing the highest and second-highest accuracies, absent from v1. Single-trial reporting remains, with no newly reported repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals. The captions do not specify the significance threshold.

E6.justification: The earlier GPT-3.5, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, extraction, and noise results are retained. v2 adds substantial backbone, cost, ablation, and error-analysis results. The new findings include exceptions to superiority: on o1-mini CLUTRR, PoT-LLM scores 58.5 versus CoT-SC's 64.6, while PoT-Symbolic scores 65.9 versus LLM-ASP's 20.2 (Table 2). These are newly reported configurations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2 introduces clearer notation for the context, question, and queried entities but retains the same problem definition and composition assumptions. Graph and path definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the graph's stated role from a task-agnostic foundation illustrated by planning to downstream relational reasoning. It also reframes the novelty claim from handling hallucinations and ambiguities through path identification to identifying query-relevant subgraphs before reasoning. The three-stage contribution and up-to-21.3% improvement claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the limitations beyond dataset-label quality to untested non-relational generalization, manual symbolic-rule construction, and latency/accuracy tradeoffs, with recommendations for choosing the two variants. New analyses distinguish path identification's benefits for LLM reasoning from its small effect on symbolic benchmark accuracy, and interpret multiple-path selection and computational efficiency.

D1.justification: v2 specifies depth-first search and documents new model settings and module-level resource consumption. It consolidates v1's conflicting temperature statements of 0 and 0.3 into 0.3, with GPT-5 defaults, without establishing that retained experiments changed. It removes the statement that code and datasets accompany supplementary materials and omits the full SPARTUN label-mapping list.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Llama 3, o1, SymBa, and hierarchical cooperative task allocation, including limited discussion of automated rule generation and task decomposition. It refines the introduction's novelty positioning, while the substantive related-work comparison with prompting and neuro-symbolic approaches remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: dataset and backbone descriptions move into Section 5.1, the noise taxonomy moves to Appendix A.1, and appendix topics and prompt collections are reordered. The limitations are rewritten and placed before the conclusion. The introduction, problem definition, and results narrative are edited, and the title loses its Path-of-Thoughts prefix.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a single-column layout with a redesigned author block. Table 1 incorporates the former appendix GPT-3.5 results and adds Llama3; new tables display reasoning-model results, costs, ablations, and errors. Prompt tables are reordered and sometimes split. Figure 2 changes from stacked to side-by-side panels with revised legends while retaining its plotted results.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 substantially strengthen evaluation of the central path-identification contribution by directly testing its removal and restricting path selection, revealing both benefits and settings with little benefit. Computational-cost measurements and expanded limitations make efficiency and applicability more assessable. These gains outweigh the dropped code/data availability disclosure and remaining reporting weaknesses, including single-trial results and broad success claims that overlook counterexamples such as o1-mini CLUTRR in Table 2.
